sourceCoverage.rationale: Six selected creator cues map to distinct analytical sections and claim IDs. The retained exact-source machine-ASR VTT was previously opened and checked for approximate alignment; later team-reuse context is attributed in prose. It is not a full listening audit.

supportingArgument.rationale: The Reader separates installed skill files, visible discovery metadata and invoked instruction bodies. This prevents the false inference that file count alone determines prompt cost or task quality.

evidenceRoles.rationale: Creator advice is attributed to the video. Anthropic and OpenAI primary documentation is now explicitly bound to the technical metadata claim and limited to product behavior. All six verification statuses remain unverified; neither vendor source measures deletion outcomes.

counterargument.rationale: Rare incident, recovery, compliance and security skills can be essential despite low invocation. Lazy or scoped discovery can reduce overhead without deleting capability, and ambiguous descriptions can cause selection errors even in small catalogs.

tradeoffs.rationale: The article weighs discovery noise and token cost against critical-skill recall, reversible retirement, ownership, scope and trust exposure, without imposing a universal deletion quota.

falsifiability.rationale: The proposed matched model, harness, task suite, permissions and compute comparison varies skill descriptors and retrieval strategy, then measures selection, false invocation, task success, latency, tokens and critical recall. It was not executed.

originalSynthesis.rationale: GhostMesh's useful inventory dimensions are visibility, invocation, criticality, owner, trust and scope; those distinctions turn the source's pruning rhetoric into a testable and reversible operating decision.

performance.rationale: No independent benchmark replicated an eighty-to-ninety-percent deletion gain or universal fifty-skill threshold. The performance discussion names measurable outcomes and confines vendor documentation to mechanism.

economics.rationale: Potential token and latency costs depend on the exact harness configuration. The article proposes measuring those costs and makes no general savings or return-on-investment claim.

threatGovernance.rationale: Reusable SOP-like skill instructions cannot grant authority, bypass approval or replace auditable tool permissions; provenance, versioning and review must travel with team-shared procedures.

gaps.rationale: The exact private manifest, transcript and timed VTT were hash-verified and selected cues inspected, but the video was not independently listened to and frames were not audited.
No controlled cross-harness deletion experiment or independent performance replication was supplied. The eighty-to-ninety-percent recommendation and universal threshold remain unverified.

decisionRationale: Accept this exact canonical article and evidence revision for Tony's separate editorial decision. The two prior P2 defects are fixed; the extended argument and four reviewed comparison routes are sound within stated ASR and outcome limits. This reviewer decision does not admit graph edges or authorize publication.
